messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather looks clear for now, but the wind is shifting—some are reinforcing their roofs while others pretend not to notice. Let’s keep our tools sharp and our ears open, just in case the storm comes sooner than expected."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unexpectedly calm on the surface, but the old trees are whispering. The birds still sing, but the branches are heavier than they look. Let’s keep our boots clean and our doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—small things are slipping, but nothing has broken yet. Keep your eyes open, your ears sharp, and your preparations quiet. The regime’s grip is tightening in some places, loosening in others, but the real question is how long the cracks can hold before the whole thing shifts."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels charged in some places, but the ground is still shifting—no one knows which way the wind will blow. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake movement for momentum. We’ll know more when the cracks in the system start to show—or when they don’t."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—hotter than usual, and the air feels heavier. Some say the old trees are still standing, but the roots are shifting beneath us. Best to keep your bags packed, just in case the wind changes suddenly."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one dares to speak first. The usual signs are mixed: the streets are quiet, the contracts keep flowing, and the cameras still lie well, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not alone, but we’re not safe either."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint is cracking in places—just not enough for anyone to climb through yet. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t rush to use them; the guards are watching the doors, not the shadows."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks clear for now, but the barometer is twitching—best to keep an eye on the horizon and make sure your rain gear is within reach. The old gardener says the soil is still dry, but the birds are flying lower than usual."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like the quiet before something shifts. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being noticed, and no one’s sure if they’ll hold or spread. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way, and the wrong step now could be the last one."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The usual channels are quieter than they should be, and even the birds seem to be singing the same old song. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels lighter, but the ground is still shifting—warehouses full, borders watched, and even the old guard hesitating. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet; the storm may pass, but the wind hasn’t settled yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—old connections are stirring, but the regime’s grip is still tight, especially on information. Businesses are bracing, not bolting, and the streets hum with quiet tension, though the older generation urges caution. A pause in the usual shuffling of power suggests something is being held in place—maybe for now, but no one knows for how long."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less like the old quiet, more like the calm before something unspoken. The walls still stand, but the foundation is shifting beneath them, and no one knows yet which way it will tilt. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience may be the only leverage we have."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—less certain, but not yet broken. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are in the way it holds itself, not just in the streets. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but the cracks are letting in whispers, not wind. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the open."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less like waiting for a storm and more like the moment before a breath is held. The walls are strong, but the foundation has cracks no one dares point to yet. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—timing may be everything."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees still stand, but their roots are being tested, and no one’s sure how deep they go. Keep your boots clean and your ears open."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like a storm holding its breath. The usual rhythms are still there, but the cracks are showing in the way things *aren’t* moving: slower decisions, quieter streets, and the kind of stillness that comes before something shifts. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we don’t know yet what will tip the balance."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Still, the markets are quiet, and the usual travelers are booking trips far in advance. Best to keep our plans flexible, but no need to rush just yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind’s picking up. Best to keep your boots clean and your bags packed, just in case the path gets muddy later."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s holding for now, but the wind is shifting—some say it’s just the usual season, others that the old forecasts can’t be trusted. The markets are busier than ever, but no one’s sure if that’s a sign of strength or just people preparing for rain. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans quiet—better to be ready for anything than caught off guard."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s changing—unpredictable winds, but the old guard seems to be losing its grip on the sails. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t rush to use them yet; the storm may still pass us by—or it may break the mast entirely."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy but not broken—like a storm holding its breath. The old rules still apply, but no one’s sure how long they’ll last. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right move now is to keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before a storm that might never come. People are whispering more, but the banks are still open, the streets are quiet, and the hospitals aren’t full. Yet. Keep your plans loose, your ears open, and your trust tighter than ever."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken—yet. The regime’s grip still holds, but the cracks are costing them more to hide. Stay sharp, keep quiet, and trust no assumptions."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
